condition: Find affordable products with useful features and positive customer feedback.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is product.price from product. The condition requires affordable products, so price is the direct attribute for affordability assessment. Starting from product, price is available on the stated path.

review.summary is a review-level text attribute on the review table. It can provide a concise expression of a customer's sentiment and mention of features, which is weakly indicative of positive customer feedback and possibly useful features, but it is not a product attribute and does not capture affordability. The signal is indirect for the product-level condition and does not connect to product.price, product.category, or product features.

The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. It provides no product attributes, price, features, rating, review text, or feedback. It cannot indicate affordability, usefulness, or positive customer feedback for products.

The signal is product.brand from product. The condition requires affordability, useful features, and positive customer feedback. Brand alone provides no evidence about price, features, or review sentiment, and the path is only product with no link to review or customer. No useful evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.category from product. The condition requires affordability, useful features, and positive customer feedback. Category alone provides no evidence about price affordability, feature usefulness, or review sentiment, and the path is only product with no link to review or customer.

The signal is product.description from product alone. It provides no price affordability, no feature usefulness, and no customer feedback. No relationship to review or customer is traversed, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is product.title from product alone. Title provides no evidence about affordability, features, or customer feedback. No price, description, category, rating, review_text, or verified information is included, and no path to review or customer is used.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. It provides a positive feedback proxy but gives no product identity, no affordability, and no feature information. Without joining to product to get price/category/description/title and without any feature-related attribute, it cannot support the condition of affordable products with useful features and positive feedback.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides no product affordability, feature, or feedback linkage; no path to product or customer, and no rating or verification. It cannot support the condition.

The signal is review.review_time from review alone. Review time does not indicate affordability, product features, or positive customer feedback. No relationship to product price, features, or rating/summary is captured, so it provides no evidence for the condition.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. It provides no information about product affordability, features, or customer feedback sentiment, and the path does not reach product or customer attributes. Therefore it cannot support the condition.

condition: Show detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: review.review_text is the review's own text attribute on the review table. It directly contains the detailed narrative of a customer's real-world product experience, satisfying the condition.

The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences, which needs review content attributes like review_text, summary, rating, review_time, verified and product context. customer_name alone provides no review text or product experience evidence and is not linked to review or product via the stated path.

The signal is product.brand from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences, which is about review content such as review_text, summary, rating, review_time, verified. Product.brand is a product attribute with no path to review content, so it provides no evidence about the detail or real-world nature of reviews.

The signal is product.category from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences, which is about review content such as review_text, summary, rating, review_time, verified. Product.category is a product-level attribute with no path to review content, so it provides no evidence about the detail or real-world nature of reviews.

The signal is product.description from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences. The signal provides product description, not review content, and is not linked to review rows via the defined path. No evidence of review text, rating, review_time, summary, verified, or customer association is present.

The signal is product.price from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences. Price is an attribute of product and provides no information about review content, review_text, summary, rating, verified, or review_time. No path connects price to review attributes, so the signal cannot support the condition.

The signal is product.title from product. The user condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences. The signal provides only a product title, with no path to review attributes such as review_text, rating, review_time, summary, verified, and no connection to customer. It does not capture review content or real-world experience evidence, so it offers no useful evidence for the condition.

The signal is review.rating from review. Rating is a numeric score and does not describe real-world product experiences. The condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world experiences, which would be captured by review_text, summary, or review_time, not by rating alone.
review.review_time is a timestamp attribute on review with no path to product or customer attributes. It provides no evidence about whether a review describes real-world product experiences.

The signal is review.summary from review. The condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences. Summary is a short attribute and does not guarantee detail or real-world experience description. No path to product or customer attributes is used, so no evidence of real-world experience is provided.

The signal is review.verified, which only indicates whether a review is verified. It does not provide any review content or description of real-world product experiences. The condition requires detailed reviews describing real-world product experiences, which would need review_text, summary, or similar content attributes, not just a boolean verified flag. Therefore the signal provides no useful evidence for the condition.

condition: Find reliable products from reputable brands with strong customer ratings.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is product.brand from product. The condition requires reputable brands and reliable products. Brand is a direct attribute of product and is the explicit brand signal needed to assess brand reputation; it is the starting entity for product reliability evaluation.

The signal is review.rating from review. The user condition requires strong customer ratings, and rating is the direct measure of customer rating strength. Path review is the starting entity, so the signal provides central, direct evidence for the rating component of the condition.

The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. It provides no product, brand, rating, or reliability information and does not connect to review or product tables, so it cannot support finding reliable products from reputable brands with strong customer ratings.

The signal is product.category from product. The user condition requires reliability, reputable brands, and strong customer ratings. Category alone provides no evidence about brand reputation, product reliability, or customer ratings, and the path starts only at product with no connection to review or customer. No useful evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.description from product. The condition requires reliability, reputable brands, and strong customer ratings. Description is a free-text product field with no direct link to brand reputation or rating evidence, and it does not connect to review.rating or review.verified or brand reputation signals. Therefore it provides no useful evidence for the stated condition.

The signal is product.price from product. Price is not a proxy for reliability, brand reputation, or customer ratings. The condition requires evidence about brand reputation and strong customer ratings; price provides no direct or indirect evidence for those criteria.

The signal is product.title from product alone. Title provides no information about brand reputation, rating strength, or reliability. No path to review or customer data is included, so the condition cannot be evaluated.

The signal is review.review_text from review alone. It provides no brand, product, or rating information and cannot identify reputable brands or strong customer ratings. No path to product or customer is included, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is review.review_time from review alone. Review time provides no information about brand reputation, product reliability, or customer rating strength. It does not connect to product.brand, product attributes, or review.rating, so it cannot support the condition.

The signal is review.summary from review alone. It provides only a textual summary of a single review with no brand, product, rating, or reliability information, and no path to product or customer. It cannot support finding reliable products from reputable brands with strong customer ratings.

The signal is review.verified from the review table alone. It provides no brand, product, or rating information and does not connect to product or customer. It cannot support finding reliable products from reputable brands with strong customer ratings.

condition: Find negative reviews highlighting defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is customer.customer_name reachable from customer only. The condition requires negative reviews with defect/quality/performance mentions, which depend on review attributes (rating, review_text, summary, verified) and product context. Customer name provides no evidence about review sentiment or defect content, and the path does not reach review or product.

The signal is product.brand from product. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Brand alone provides no information about review sentiment, review text content, or product quality issues, and the path starts at product without connecting to review attributes like rating, review_text, summary, or verified. No evidence linking brand to negative review characteristics is present in the schema.

The signal is product.category from product. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Category alone provides no information about review sentiment, review text content, or product quality issues, and the signal path starts from product without connecting to review attributes like rating, review_text, summary, or verified. No evidence linking category to negative review content is present in the schema.

The signal is product.description from product. The user condition requires negative reviews highlighting defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. The signal provides only product description text, with no path to review.rating, review.review_text, review.summary, or review.verified, and no connection to review content. Therefore it cannot provide evidence about negative reviews or their content.

The signal is product.price from product. The user condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Price is not a review attribute and does not indicate sentiment or defect mentions. No path connects price to review_text, rating, or verified, so the signal provides no evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.title from product. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Product title alone provides no information about review sentiment or defect content, and the signal path starts at product with no connection to review attributes like rating, review_text, summary, or verified. No evidence of negativity or defects is reachable from product.title.

The signal is only review.rating from the review table. Rating alone does not indicate whether a review highlights defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance, and the schema provides no mapping from rating values to those specific themes. No review_text, summary, or other content attributes are included, so the signal cannot capture the required negative defect/quality/performance focus.

The signal is only review.review_text from the review table with no path to product or customer. It provides no evidence about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance, and no way to identify negative reviews.

review.review_time is a timestamp attribute on review with no relationship to sentiment, defects, quality, or performance. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects/poor quality/disappointing performance, which depends on review content (review_text, summary, rating, verified) and product/customer context, not on when the review was written. The signal provides no evidence toward the condition.

The signal is review.summary from review alone. The condition requires identifying negative reviews about defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance. Summary alone provides no sentiment or defect indication and no link to rating or review_text, so it cannot evidence the condition.

The signal is review.verified, which only indicates whether a review is verified. It does not capture review content or sentiment, so it provides no evidence about negative reviews highlighting defects, poor quality, or disappointing performance.

condition: Identify customers who write thoughtful, balanced, and informative reviews.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: The signal is review.review_text from the review table. Review text can contain content indicative of thoughtfulness, balance, and informativeness, but the signal is only the raw text with no derived features, length, or sentiment cues, so it provides useful but incomplete evidence for identifying customers who write thoughtful, balanced, informative reviews.
Signal is only customer.customer_name with path customer. No review attributes or review text are included, so it provides no evidence about thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness of reviews.

The signal is product.brand reachable from product via review.product_id. Brand is a product attribute and provides no information about whether a review is thoughtful, balanced, and informative, nor about the customer who wrote it. No path connects brand to review content or customer writing style.

The signal is product.category from product, reached via review.product_id. Category is a product attribute and provides no information about whether a review is thoughtful, balanced, and informative, nor about the customer who wrote it. No review content or customer attributes are involved, so the signal carries no evidence for the condition.

The signal is product.description from product, reached via product. The user condition is about customers who write thoughtful, balanced, and informative reviews. Product description provides information about the product, not about the customer or the review content/quality. No path connects product.description to review attributes like review_text, rating, verified, or to customer. Therefore the signal gives no evidence for identifying customers with thoughtful, balanced, informative reviews.

The signal is product.price reachable from product via path product. The user condition requires identifying customers who write thoughtful, balanced, and informative reviews. Product price provides no evidence about review thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness, nor about the customer author. No relationship to review content or customer writing style is captured.

The signal is product.title from product, reached via product path. The user condition requires identifying customers who write thoughtful, balanced, informative reviews. Product title provides no information about review quality or customer writing style, and the signal does not involve review attributes or customer identity. No plausible evidence for the condition.

The signal is review.rating from review alone. Rating is a numeric score and does not capture thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness of review text. No path to review_text, summary, or verified, and no customer linkage is used, so it provides no evidence for the condition.
review.review_time is a timestamp attribute on review with no path to customer or product content. It provides no evidence about thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness of review text.

The signal is review.summary from review. The condition requires identifying customers who write thoughtful, balanced, and informative reviews. The summary attribute alone provides no evidence of thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness, and the signal is not linked to customer via review.customer_id. No useful schema evidence is present.

review.verified is a boolean flag about purchase verification; it does not capture thoughtfulness, balance, or informativeness of review content. No path to review_text, summary, rating, or customer attributes is used, so the signal provides no evidence for the condition.
